title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between life and death there is a library. Its shelves go on forever. Every book provides a chance to try another life you could have lived.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship teaching programmers the principles, patterns, and practices of writing clean, maintainable code.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: From the Big Bang to black holes, Hawking explores the structure, origin, development, and eventual fate of the universe.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A magical story about Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy, who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure as extravagant as any ever found.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas
description: From journeyman to master, this book helps programmers examine the core of the software development process and build better software.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: A personal voyage through the universe and time, exploring 15 billion years of cosmic evolution that transformed matter into consciousness.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: A story of racial injustice and the loss of innocence in the American South, told through the eyes of young Scout Finch.

title: Design Patterns
author: Gang of Four
description: Elements of reusable object-oriented software — a catalog of 23 classic design patterns every developer should know.

title: The Gene
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: An intimate history of the gene — the basic unit of heredity, how it was discovered, and how it will transform medicine and humanity.

author: George Orwell
description: A chilling dystopian novel depicting a totalitarian society where Big Brother watches every move and the truth is whatever the Party says it is.

title: You Don't Know JS
author: Kyle Simpson
description: A deep dive into the core mechanisms of the JavaScript language, covering closures, scopes, prototypes, and async patterns.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: Dawkins argues that the gene is the fundamental unit of selection in evolution, introducing the concept of the meme along the way.
